assumptions: The family connection provides practical access to propose a bounded pilot, but it does not imply operational adoption, payment, exclusivity, or repeat use.

The venture consistently preserves the stated no-custody boundary and leaves transport, storage, testing, dismantling, preparation for reuse, and waste handling to appropriately authorized and insured counterparties.
Suitable professional buyers and authorized operators can be approached for the pilot, while their responsiveness, pricing, contractual terms, and willingness to participate remain unknown.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid and repeated work orders from both the family installer and at least one unrelated installer; an activity-based record of fee, founder time, partner costs, exception costs, contribution margin, and turnaround time; a Polish legal opinion covering classification, advisory liability, documentation, and handoff boundaries; binding or trial SLAs from authorized operators and professional buyers; and completed-route evidence showing transfer rates, disputes, returns, and repeat usage.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Moving the disposition decision before removal is a coherent response to the product-versus-waste boundary: it creates a moment to assemble title and condition evidence before regulated options narrow. The insight is useful and testable, but the packet does not establish that this checkpoint is a missing service rather than work already performed by installers, buyers, or authorized operators.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Classification, documentation, liability, and uncertain residual value plausibly create pain at replacement events. However, no installer has authorized or paid for the checkpoint, no current handling cost has been quantified, and incumbents may already provide an adequate route, leaving willingness to pay highly uncertain.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A fixed workflow fee independent of salvage is more disciplined than relying on speculative resale, and the no-inventory design limits capital exposure. Yet price, volume, conversion, fully loaded service cost, partner charges, exception burden, repeat rate, margin, CAC, and payback are all unvalidated; manual multi-party coordination and low-density removals could consume the fee.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: One equipment class, one dense service area, and planned replacement work form a sharply bounded pilot beachhead. The packet provides no evidence that commercial string-inverter removals are sufficiently frequent, homogeneous, or valuable to support an economically meaningful standalone segment.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: The proposed checkpoint is not backed by exclusive supply, a contractual mandate, protected rights, or a proprietary standard. PV CYCLE and SecondSol already cover substantial parts of compliance, collection, testing, repair, resale, logistics, and recycling, and installers or those incumbents could reproduce an upstream evidence workflow.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven workflow could extend to additional installer clusters, regions, equipment classes, and portfolio owners, with accumulated route data potentially reducing later decision costs. Each adjacency may introduce different classification, testing, safety, warranty, buyer, and logistics requirements, so expansion is plausible but not yet demonstrably easy.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Serial-level outcomes could eventually become a useful data asset, but no proprietary dataset, exclusive partner terms, switching costs, workflow lock-in, certification, or network effect exists. The service is currently a replicable coordination process exposed to integration by larger downstream operators.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A single auditable route record and pre-removal bid gate could improve convenience and reduce mishandling risk. There is no measured comparison against the installer's current process on speed, cost, compliance quality, recovery value, or liability reduction, and the need to coordinate multiple counterparties may offset the convenience.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Rising PV waste and reuse activity, alongside demanding documentation and immature second-hand assessment guidance, creates a timely need for better routing evidence. The same immature guidance increases grading, safety, and liability uncertainty, so momentum is favorable but not unambiguously so.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The family installer creates a low-cost route to propose and observe an initial pilot in a real workflow. It is neither a paid commitment nor evidence of acquisition beyond that relationship; reaching unrelated installers may require trust-heavy sales, integration effort, and proof that incumbents do not already solve the problem.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The one-class, one-region, no-custody design contains capital and operational scope and fits the founder's analytical and automation strengths. Material execution risks remain in legal advice boundaries, document accuracy, partner response times, warranty and dispute allocation, heterogeneous title status, low event density, and part-time multi-party coordination.

highest_value_structural_change: Convert the proposed one-off checkpoint into a contracted portfolio-wide workflow embedded in installer work-order systems, backed by an authorized-operator and professional-buyer response-time SLA and, if obtainable, insurer or processor endorsement. This would create recurring paid volume, a more defensible control point, and systematic outcome data rather than relying on ad hoc coordination.
main_structural_strength: The pre-removal, no-custody gate is a bounded and capital-light way to test whether better evidence and routing can create value while authorized partners retain regulated physical activities.
primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence that installers will pay repeatedly for the checkpoint or that sparse removal volume, partner coordination, legal and insurance allocation, and exception handling can produce attractive contribution economics; the proposed control point is also non-exclusive and readily replicable.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: PV CYCLE and SecondSol already provide much of the compliance, collection, testing, repair, resale, logistics, and recycling stack, while PV CYCLE describes treatment as high-volume and low-return; this weakens both the claimed service gap and the prospect of wide margins without a contracted upstream mandate.
